S034-01.notes: Spring keeps flowing even in driest summers -> inexhaustible. Contaminated/costly unrelated; seasonal contradicts.

S034-02.notes: 3 of 4 wells struck water, suggesting success -> auspicious (promising). Ominous opposite; negligible/ambiguous contradict clear positive results.

S034-03.notes: Lime clasts once thought careless-mixing flaws may enable self-healing. Matches 2023 MIT study (Seymour, Masic et al., Science Advances). B/C/D unsupported.

S034-04.notes: Chase & Simon-style result: expert advantage vanishes on random boards, so advantage stems from pattern recognition. A contradicted by random-board result; B, D unsupported.

flags: minor: B is the only choice that compares both the medians and the longest distances across species, a mild structural cue, though this is inherent to a two-part conclusion
S034-05.notes: Conclusion has two parts: A's median > B's; B's max > A's max. Only B gives both comparisons. A omits A's longest; C omits median comparison; D omits median comparison.

S034-06.notes: Replication found smaller, inconsistent differences -> evidence weaker than claimed. B overstates reverse; C (sample size) not mentioned; A contradicts.

S034-07.notes: Only C gives the reason (rejection by U.S. schools). Facts accurate: Coleman earned FAI license 1921 in France.

flags: minor: 'However,' would be the most natural contrast transition; 'Conversely' works since the second sentence describes the reverse effect (ocean heat weakening rather than strengthening), but some may find it slightly imprecise
S034-08.notes: First sentence: warm water strengthens storms. Second: stalled storm cools water and weakens itself -> contrast. Similarly, For example, Thus all imply agreement/consequence; only Conversely signals contrast.

S034-09.notes: 'The children's choir's performance' -- plural irregular possessive children's + singular possessive choir's before performance. A 'childrens'' wrong; B lacks possessive on choirs (would need choirs'); C 'childrens' wrong.

S034-10.notes: 'By the time ... was completed in 1936' (past) requires past perfect progressive 'had been working'. Facts accurate (construction 1931-1936).
